basis: Autoantibodies inhibit factor VIII, causing an acquired coagulation disorder.
Lysosomal lipid storage; neurologic deterioration and hepatic disease in 80-99%; hearing impairment in 30-79%. Splenic/marrow storage alone does not establish dysfunction.
Complement-system immunodeficiency; infections and organ-specific autoimmune complications are separate diseases or subtype-dependent.
Cleft lip/palate and labial pits define the shared oral phenotype. Limb contractures belong principally to the popliteal pterygium subtype.
Benign neoplasm arising in ocular structures, including eyelids and lacrimal glands.
Carcinoma originates in the maxillary sinus, an upper-airway structure.
Hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma; compressive visual impairment and visual field defects occur in 30-79%. Other neurologic complications are occasional.
Adenoma of the anterior pituitary gland. Visual damage is not established as common across this histologic category.
Benign epithelial neoplasm confined to skin.
Hereditary gallbladder disorder; the gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
Skeletal dysplasia with short bones, joint stiffness and hip abnormalities. Airway, ocular and valvular disease vary by subtype; common functional damage across the umbrella is unestablished.
Carcinoma originates in the penis, a reproductive organ outside the axes; cutaneous or urinary origin is not specified.
Varicella-zoster reactivation causes ganglionitis or radiculitis without a cutaneous eruption.
The defining triad comprises shortened digits, a cardiac ventricular septal defect and deafness.
Congenital lifelong joint contractures and skeletal deformities; gait impairment is mechanical. Neurologic findings are occasional.
Core features include macroglossia, abdominal wall defects and lateralized overgrowth; hyperinsulinism is a major diagnostic criterion. Tumor predisposition does not establish organ damage.
Congenital structural duplication of the colon.
Acquired testicular failure includes loss of gonadal endocrine function.
Congenital viral infection; most infants lack manifestations. Anomalies described in one exceptional case do not establish common organ damage.

Folate-metabolism disorder with combined immunodeficiency and megaloblastic anemia. Intellectual disability, seizures and hippocampal hypoplasia reported in 1/1 assessed; frequency evidence is sparse.
Congenital narrowing of the pulmonary cardiac valve; this is a cardiovascular lesion.
Defective sweat glands and sparse hair accompany defining hypodontia and malformed teeth. Endocrine abnormalities are occasional; fever reflects impaired sweating.
Epithelial tumor originates in the vermiform appendix; an endocrine subtype does not define the umbrella.
Congenital lower-lip fistula lined by labial mucosa, sometimes communicating with salivary glands. Infection is only a possible complication.
Microcephaly/intellectual disability and digital skeletal malformations define the syndrome. Optic atrophy and nail hypoplasia each occur in 30-79%; cardiac defects are occasional.
